title: D-NOVA: In-Storage Retrieval Accelerator via Dual-Bound 3D NAND-Optimized Similarity Search with Vector Adaptation
event_hint: D-NOVA: an in-storage vector retrieval accelerator for RAG that embeds IVF-based similarity search directly into 3D NAND arrays using Dual-bound Tight Similarity Sensing (DTS) and a contrastive vector adapter (MICRO 2026).
problem: Dense vector retrieval in RAG is the primary latency/energy bottleneck. Existing in-storage/near-storage accelerators (SmartSSD, RAGX, REIS) still rely on host/embedded processors for final re-ranking; in REIS this INT8 re-ranking step accounts for nearly 70% of total retrieval time, dominated by multi-level cell read latency and data movement to the embedded processor, creating a new memory wall.
mechanism: D-NOVA executes an IVF-based hierarchical retrieval pipeline entirely inside the NAND array. It introduces Dual-bound Tight Similarity Sensing (DTS), a distance metric that reformulates vector retrieval as a query-dependent threshold search over ordered V_TH levels using complement sensing and compact scoring within the NAND string. A lightweight contrastive adapter maps embedding vectors into a DTS-friendly domain to recover near-software recall. Only compact scores/metadata leave the array; full embeddings never move off-array. D-NOVA reuses existing page-buffer structures in binary pass/fail mode, preserving standard QLC read/program compatibility and achieving SLC-like read latency at QLC density.

evidence.claim: D-NOVA is up to 41.7x faster and 71x more energy-efficient than a CPU baseline, and achieves 12.13x higher throughput while being up to 1.26x more energy-efficient than state-of-the-art in-storage RAG accelerators.
evidence.baseline: CPU baseline; state-of-the-art in-storage RAG accelerators
evidence.condition: abstract headline; per-workload breakdown in results

evidence.claim: In prior in-storage accelerators, the off-array INT8 re-ranking step accounts for nearly 70% of total retrieval time, dominated by MLC read latency and data movement to the embedded processor.
evidence.condition: REIS-style in-storage accelerators with controller-side re-ranking
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 2 - REIS analysis

evidence.claim: D-NOVA and D-NOVA-F sustain roughly 481-679x of the CPU QPS and about 42.7-67.9x of the NSP baseline throughput; relative to REIS, D-NOVA/D-NOVA-F improve throughput by ~4.3-6.1x and D-NOVA-XF reaches ~8.6-12.1x higher QPS.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 12 - Throughput Improvement

evidence.claim: Compared to REIS, D-NOVA reduces latency by 3.01-3.79x, D-NOVA-F by 3.80-4.99x, and D-NOVA-XF by 5.98-7.53x, with additional energy savings of 6-27% by avoiding off-array final re-ranking.

Simulated on QLC 3D NAND (128 WLs/string, 8.5V window, PTM-MG 14nm) using Spectre circuit simulation and Monte Carlo V_TH variation modeling; config: PCIe 4.0x4 host, 8 flash channels (16 GB/s total), 8 dies/ch, 12 planes/die, ~1 TB/s inter-plane H-Tree bandwidth; shared accumulator adds 0.023 mm^2/plane (<1.5% of 1.476 mm^2 plane area) synthesized at ASAP7 7nm.
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: PDF Page 9 - Tables 1 & 2; PDF Page 12 - 6.7 Overhead

evaluation_context: Simulated in-storage NVMe SSD subsystem (not silicon). QLC 3D NAND (128 WLs/string), 8 flash channels at 2.0 GB/s/channel (16 GB/s total), 8 dies/channel, 12 planes/die, ~1 TB/s inter-plane H-Tree bandwidth, PCIe 4.0x4 host interface. Circuit-level validation via Spectre 19.1 (PTM-MG 14nm) with Monte Carlo V_TH mismatch and QLC drift modeling; accumulator synthesized with ASAP7 7nm at 1 GHz. Workloads: BEIR/NQ, HotpotQA, synthetic dataset (16GB-120GB); embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and all-mpnet-base-v2. Baselines: CPU-IVF (FAISS IVF-Flat on dual-socket 128-core server, 1.5TB DDR4), NSP baseline, REIS.
limitations: Results are simulation-based (cycle-level SSD model plus Spectre/Monte Carlo circuit simulation), not measurements from fabricated silicon. Read latency/energy parameters are rescaled from prior measured NAND data (294.9 nJ/page read, 30us SLC / 140us QLC). Absolute end-to-end RAG serving latency (including LLM generation) is not reported; metrics focus on retrieval stage. Endurance/write-amplification impact of DTS sensing on QLC cells is not quantified in the visible evidence. DTS sensing resolution degrades at larger simultaneous-cell count m, a tradeoff tuned per config.
project_relevance: D-NOVA is a NAND-centric in-storage compute design that pushes vector search into the flash array, directly relevant to whether 3D NAND can take on AI-serving storage-hierarchy roles (RAG retrieval) beyond bulk storage. For the project card it is a simulation-stage architecture study showing how in-array sensing can convert NAND density into retrieval throughput/energy gains; it is not a product or deployed system. The QLC-density-at-SLC-latency claim touches the storage-media density/bandwidth/latency questions.
source_notes: arXiv preprint 2607.17538v1 (20 Jul 2026), to appear MICRO 2026; FETCHED primary source; authors from UC San Diego.
All performance numbers are simulation-based (cycle-level SSD simulator + Spectre/Monte Carlo), not silicon measurements.
Baselines explicitly named: CPU-IVF (FAISS on 128-core server), NSP near-storage processor, REIS in-storage; D-NOVA variants D-NOVA/D-NOVA-F/D-NOVA-XF differ by (m1,m2,m3) multi-cell sensing config.
